note: Concession-run Los Padres NF campground at the end of Arroyo Seco Road, in oak woodland near the Arroyo Seco River. The RV sites are in the modern loop, which has the flush toilets, coin showers and water; the primitive loops are tent sites with vault toilets. Some sites are level and long enough for big rigs. Day-use river beach nearby. --Claude
summary: Arroyo Seco: rec.gov 231958, 21 RV sites of 39, $42 single / $82 double, no hookups, showers and flush toilets in the modern loop, year-round, 2-night weekend / 3-night holiday minimums. Riverview -> not waterfront recommended. Pin ~890 m off (on the hillside across the river) -> RV loop centroid 36.23370,-121.48514. Open; the Monterey RD fire-closure order closes the road beyond, not the campground.
flags: PIN MOVE ~890 m: stored 36.23972,-121.47861 (rec.gov facility point, on the open grass hillside north of the river) -> 36.23370,-121.48514 (centroid of the 21 RV-site points in loop MCML).

WATERFRONT: stored 'riverview' (not --AWH; evidence said 'open ground, water visible') -> recommend 'not waterfront'. On Esri imagery the RV loop is in continuous oak woodland. The nearest RV sites (030 at 36.23450,-121.48507; 032; 033) and the walk-to tent sites 027-029 (36.2345-36.2346,-121.4845) are ~80-130 m from the river channel. Between them are a wooded strip and the camp road / day-use area. No sightline was found. The river beach is a day-use area. All sites are sold nightly on rec.gov. A seasonal pond basin (green, algae-covered on imagery) lies ~50 m east of RV sites 015/017/023 behind trees, and rec.gov says its 'water levels depend on the season'; it does not earn a value.
FEES conflict: rec.gov charges $42/$82 (2026 and 2027 rate tables); the FS page still says $40/$70. Wrote rec.gov.
VEHICLES conflict: rec.gov says '8 people and 2 vehicles' per site; the FS page says 'only one vehicle per single site'. Wrote rec.gov's 2 included, $10 each extra.
